messages:
maria: Heads-up — since last deploy the us-west-2 spot GPU nodegroup has steady interruptions, ~6-8% ephemeral this morning. noticing backlog on batch-job pods after nodes get terminated.

kai: Ugh. Are cluster-autoscaler logs showing scale-up delays or is it just capacity shortage?

maria: Scale-up kicks but new spot nodes take longer than usual to become schedulable (initcontainer image pulls + nvidia driver probe). CA marks them as ready but kubelet reports NotReady for ~40-60s, so pods are requeued.

devops-bot: [event] Spot interruption received for i-0abc... in us-west-2 (2m notice)

ash: Two quick wins: 1) reduce init container image size / use local disk cache for drivers, 2) make our GPU workloads tolerate transient requeues via topologySpread and PodDisruptionBudgets.

ryan: Also consider mixed-capacity fallback: have a small dedicated GPU pool (3-5 nodes) labeled dedicated=true that non-spot-critical pods can fall back to. Autoscaler can maintain minimum for it.

maria: Agreed. Another blocker — we currently drain in the interruption hook but some pods are non-evictable (no toleration for spot-taint), so they get stuck and cause NodeNotReady state to persist until IMDS termination. Looking at a webhook to add toleration or to migrate critical pods into dedicated pool automatically.

kai: We tried a mutation webhook before; it was brittle. Simpler: mark spot nodes with taint node.kubernetes.io/spot=true:NoSchedule and use tolerations for batch/gpu-spot podspecs, then use pod-affinity to prefer spot but allow fallback. That way drain succeeds because critical pods tolerate the taint and get evicted (or rescheduled) in time.

maria: Example eviction sequence I'm proposing (in interruption lambda):
```bash
kubectl annotate node $NODE spot-interruption=true
kubectl taint nodes $NODE spot-draining=true:NoSchedule || true
kubectl cordon $NODE
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=120
```
This lets us surface the node to console, taint to avoid new pods, then drain quickly.

ash: Two caveats: 1) drain will fail for pods without PDB allowances > 0, so ensure PDBs are configured for latency-sensitive replicas; 2) 120s grace may be too short for large model loads, maybe 300s for long-running inferences.

ryan: For autoscaler tuning: adjust expander to priority and set balance-similar-node-group to true; also set scale-up-delay after failure to 30s and use max-node-provision-time around 10m for spot pools. Helps when spot capacity is highly variable.

devops-bot: [recommendation] Detected high image-pull times for gpu-init: consider ECR / regional mirroring.

maria: Cost trade-off note: if we keep a small dedicated pool for fallback we pay fixed cost but reduce latency/regret during preemption. math says 3 x a100 dedicated (~$X/hr) vs 6 spot nodes with 8% preemptions -> expected extra retries & ops > dedicated delta after ~2000 hr of workload. (I'll attach calc later).

kai: Ops ask: add metrics we can alert on: spot-interruption-rate, average drain duration, %pods evicted vs stuck, CA pending scaleups. If any > threshold auto-promote one dedicated node (label flip) and trigger a quick rollout to move critical pods.

maria: I'll prototype the interruption lambda that annotates, taints, cordons, and calls kubectl drain, plus a reconciler that watches annotated nodes and triggers label-based migration into dedicated pool. Will post a draft with diffs.

ash: Nice. Also document runbook: how to force promote a dedicated node, how to rollback autoscaler changes, and how to inspect stuck pods (kubectl describe pod + events). Keep runbook under eng-infra/docops.

ryan: +1. If you want I can own the autoscaler parameter PR.

maria: Thanks @ryan — assign to you once I push the RFC. For now I opened a short-term mitigation: added toleration to gpu-job DaemonSet and bumped drain grace to 240s. Will monitor. :thumbsup:

devops-bot: [info] Thread closed by automation: follow-up in 24h for metrics check.
